title.zh: 卷一百二十一 列傳第九 公主
title.raw: 卷一百二十一 列傳第九 公主 Volume 121 Biographies 9: Princesses

sentences.zh: 明制，皇姑曰大長公主，皇姊妹曰長公主，皇女曰公主，俱授金冊，祿二千石，婿曰駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Under Ming institutions, the emperor's paternal aunt was called Grand Senior Princess, the emperor's sisters Senior Princess, and the emperor's daughters Princess; all were granted golden registers, stipends of two thousand shi, and their husbands were titled Commandant of Horse Escort.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming regulations, the emperor's paternal aunt bore the title Grand Senior Princess, his sisters Senior Princess, and his daughters Princess. Each received a golden investiture register, an income equivalent to two thousand shi, and her husband held the title Commandant of Horse Escort.

sentences.zh: 親王女曰郡主，郡王女曰縣主，孫女曰郡君，曾孫女曰縣君，玄孫女曰鄉君，婿皆儀賓。

translations.literal: Daughters of imperial princes of the first rank were called Commandery Mistress, daughters of princes of the second rank District Mistress, granddaughters Commandery Lady, great-granddaughters District Lady, and great-great-granddaughters Village Lady; their husbands were all Ceremonial Guests.
translations.idiomatic: A prince of the first rank's daughter was a Commandery Mistress; a prince of the second rank's daughter, a District Mistress; a granddaughter a Commandery Lady; a great-granddaughter a District Lady; and a great-great-granddaughter a Village Lady. Their husbands all held the title Ceremonial Guest.

sentences.zh: 郡主祿八百石，余遞減有差。

translations.literal: The Commandery Mistress received eight hundred shi in stipend; the rest were reduced in graduated differences.
translations.idiomatic: A Commandery Mistress drew eight hundred shi; lower ranks received proportionally less.

sentences.zh: 郡主以下，恩禮既殺，無足書者。

translations.literal: Below the Commandery Mistress, favor and ritual were already diminished, not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: Below the rank of Commandery Mistress, patronage and ceremonial honors were too slight to warrant individual entries.

sentences.zh: 今依前史例，作《公主傳》，而駙馬都尉附焉。

translations.literal: Now, following the precedents of earlier histories, the 《Biographies of Princesses》 is composed, with the Commandants of Horse Escort appended.
translations.idiomatic: Following earlier dynastic histories, we compose the 《Biographies of Princesses》, with the Commandants of Horse Escort appended thereto.

sentences.zh: 仁祖二女太祖十六女

translations.literal: Two daughters of the founding ancestor; sixteen daughters of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor's two daughters; Taizu's sixteen daughters.

sentences.zh: 〈（福成慶陽二主附）〉

translations.literal: (With the two princesses of Fucheng and Qingyang appended.)〉
translations.idiomatic: with the Fucheng and Qingyang princesses appended.)〉

sentences.zh: 興宗四女成祖五女仁宗七女宣宗二女英宗八女景帝一女憲宗五女孝宗三女睿宗二女世宗五女穆宗六女神宗十女光宗九女熹宗二女莊烈帝六女仁祖二女

translations.literal: Four daughters of the Progenitor of the Revival; five daughters of Chengzu; seven of Renzong; two of Xuanzong; eight of Yingzong; one of the Jing Emperor; five of Xianzong; three of Xiaozong; two of Ruizong; five of Shizong; six of Muzong; ten of Shenzong; nine of Guangzong; two of Xizong; six of the Zhuanglie Emperor; two of the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Progenitor of the Revival had four daughters; Chengzu five; Renzong seven; Xuanzong two; Yingzong eight; the Jing Emperor one; Xianzong five; Xiaozong three; Ruizong two; Shizong five; Muzong six; Shenzong ten; Guangzong nine; Xizong two; the Zhuanglie Emperor six; and the founding ancestor two.

sentences.zh: 仁祖二女

translations.literal: Two daughters of the founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor had two daughters.

sentences.zh: 太原長公主，淳皇后所生，嫁王七一，早卒。

translations.literal: The Senior Princess of Taiyuan, born to Empress Chun, married Wang Qiyi and died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Princess of Taiyuan, daughter of Empress Chun, married Wang Qiyi and died young.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年追冊，並贈七一榮祿大夫駙馬都尉，遣使具衣冠改葬於盱眙。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu she was posthumously enfeoffed, and Qiyi was also granted the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Commandant of Horse Escort; envoys were dispatched with full raiment to rebury her at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 she was posthumously enfeoffed, and Qiyi was granted the rank of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and the title Commandant of Horse Escort. Envoys were sent with full funeral regalia to rebury her at Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 曹國長公主，太原主母妹，嫁李貞。

translations.literal: The Senior Princess of the State of Cao, younger sister of the mother of the Princess of Taiyuan, married Li Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Senior Princess of Cao, younger sister of the Taiyuan princess's mother, married Li Zhen.

sentences.zh: 主性純孝，助貞理家尤勤儉，早卒。

translations.literal: The princess was by nature pure in filial piety; she helped Zhen manage the household with especial diligence and thrift, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was deeply filial and helped Zhen run the household with exceptional diligence and frugality. She too died young.

sentences.zh: 貞攜子文忠避兵，依太祖於滁陽。

translations.literal: Zhen took his son Wenzhong and fled the warfare, attaching himself to Taizu at Chuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fled the fighting with his son Wenzhong and joined Taizu at Chuyang.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年二月追冊主為孝親公主，封貞恩親侯駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongwu the princess was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Filial Kinship, and Zhen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gracious Kinship and Commandant of Horse Escort.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Hongwu year 1 the princess was posthumously enfeoffed as Princess of Filial Kinship, and Zhen was made Marquis of Gracious Kinship and Commandant of Horse Escort.

sentences.zh: 先是，兵亂，主未葬，命有司具禮葬於李氏先墓。

translations.literal: Earlier, amid the military turmoil, the princess had not been buried; he ordered the officials to prepare rites and bury her at the Li clan's ancestral tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, amid the chaos of war, the princess had remained unburied. He ordered the authorities to conduct a proper funeral and inter her in the Li family graveyard.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「公主祠堂碑亭，其制悉視功臣之贈爵為王者。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "For the princess's ancestral hall and stele pavilion, the regulations shall all follow those for meritorious ministers enfeoffed as kings."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The princess's ancestral hall and memorial stele pavilion shall follow the same regulations as those granted to meritorious ministers enfeoffed as kings."

sentences.zh: 三年改冊主隴西長公主。

translations.literal: In the third year her title was changed to Senior Princess of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 her title was changed to Senior Princess of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 五年，以文忠貴，加冊曹國長公主，並進貞右柱國曹國公。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, because Wenzhong had risen in eminence, she was further enfeoffed as Senior Princess of the State of Cao, and Zhen was advanced to Right Pillar of the State and Duke of the State of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, as Wenzhong's standing had risen, she was further enfeoffed as Senior Princess of Cao, and Zhen was promoted to Right Pillar of the State and Duke of Cao.

sentences.zh: 貞性孝友恭謹。

translations.literal: Zhen was by nature filial, friendly, respectful, and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was filial, cordial, respectful, and discreet by nature.

sentences.zh: 初，文忠守嚴州，屢以征伐事出，皆委貞權掌軍務。

translations.literal: At first, when Wenzhong held Yanzhou, he repeatedly went out on campaign and entrusted Zhen with full authority over military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhong was stationed at Yanzhou, he was often away on campaign and left Zhen in full charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 文忠克桐廬，以所俘卒送嚴。

translations.literal: When Wenzhong took Tonglu, he sent the captured soldiers to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenzhong captured Tonglu, he sent the prisoners of war to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴城空虛，俘卒謀叛去。

translations.literal: The city of Yan was empty; the captive soldiers plotted to rebel and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was lightly garrisoned, and the prisoners plotted a mutiny and escape.

sentences.zh: 貞饗其眾，醉而縛之，以歸應天。

translations.literal: Zhen feasted their company, bound them when drunk, and brought them back to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen entertained the men, waited until they were drunk, bound them, and escorted them to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，累授官如子爵，賜甲第西華門玄津橋之西。

translations.literal: Taizu commended him, repeatedly promoted him to offices like those of a viscount, and granted him a fine mansion west of the Xuanjin Bridge at Xihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised him, repeatedly promoted him to ranks comparable to a viscount's, and granted him a fine residence west of the Xuanjin Bridge at Xihua Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝數臨幸，太子諸王時往起居，親重無與比。

translations.literal: The emperor often visited in person; the crown prince and the princes frequently came to inquire after his health—none was held in such intimate esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited him often; the crown prince and other princes called on him regularly. No one else enjoyed such personal favor.

sentences.zh: 晚歲尤折節謙抑，嘗曰：「富貴而忘貧賤，君子不為也。」

translations.literal: In his later years he was especially self-restraining and humble, and once said: "To forget poverty and low station once one is rich and honored—this a gentleman does not do."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he became especially modest and self-effacing. He once said, "A gentleman does not forget poverty and humble origins once he has grown rich and eminent."

sentences.zh: 十二年冬卒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of year 12.

sentences.zh: 贈隴西王，謚恭獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Longxi, with the posthumous title Respectful and Offering.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as King of Longxi with the temple name Respectful and Offering.

sentences.zh: 文忠自有傳。

translations.literal: Wenzhong has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhong has a separate biography elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 太祖十六女

translations.literal: Sixteen daughters of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's sixteen daughters

sentences.zh: 臨安公主，洪武九年下嫁李祺，韓國公善長子也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Lin'an, in the ninth year of Hongwu married Li Qi, eldest son of the Duke of Han, Li Shanchang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Lin'an married Li Qi in Hongwu year 9. Qi was the eldest son of Li Shanchang, Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 是時始定公主婚禮，先期賜駙馬冠誥並朝服，儀從甚盛。

translations.literal: At that time the wedding rites for princesses were first fixed; beforehand the commandant was granted cap, patent, and court robes, and his ceremonial escort was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: This was when the wedding protocol for princesses was first established. The commandant was given his cap, patent of appointment, and court robes in advance, and his ceremonial escort was splendid.

sentences.zh: 主執婦道甚備。

translations.literal: The princess observed the wife's way with great completeness.
translations.idiomatic: The princess fulfilled every duty expected of a wife.

sentences.zh: 祺，功臣子，帝長婿，頗委任之。

translations.literal: Qi, as son of a meritorious minister and the emperor's eldest son-in-law, was quite entrusted with responsibilities.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of a founding minister and the emperor's eldest son-in-law, Qi received considerable trust and responsibility.

sentences.zh: 四方水旱，每命祺往振濟。

translations.literal: Whenever flood or drought struck the four quarters, Qi was ordered to go and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever floods or droughts struck the realm, the emperor sent Qi to distribute relief.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，善長坐事死。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Shanchang died on account of his offense.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 Shanchang was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 祺前卒，主至永樂十九年薨。

translations.literal: Qi had died earlier; the princess lived until the nineteenth year of Yongle, when she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had died earlier. The princess lived until Yongle year 19.

sentences.zh: 寧國公主，孝慈皇后生。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ning, born to Empress Xiaoci.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ning, daughter of Empress Xiaoci.

sentences.zh: 洪武十一年下嫁梅殷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Hongwu she married Mei Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 11 she married Mei Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷字伯殷，汝南侯思祖從子也，天性恭謹，有謀略，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Yin, style name Boyin, was a nephew of Marquis Sizu of Runan; by nature he was respectful and cautious, possessed stratagems, and was skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, courtesy name Boyin, was a nephew of Marquis Sizu of Runan. Naturally respectful and cautious, he was resourceful and skilled in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 太祖十六女諸駙馬中，尤愛殷。

translations.literal: Among all the commandants of Taizu's sixteen daughters, he especially favored Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the husbands of Taizu's sixteen daughters, the emperor favored Yin most.

sentences.zh: 時李文忠以上公典國學，而殷視山東學政，賜敕褒美，謂殷精通經史，堪為儒宗。

translations.literal: At the time Li Wenzhong as senior duke directed the National Academy, while Yin oversaw Shandong educational administration; an edict of praise was granted, saying Yin was thoroughly versed in the classics and histories and could serve as patriarch of the ru.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Wenzhong, as a senior duke, directed the National Academy, Yin oversaw education in Shandong. The emperor issued a commendatory edict declaring Yin thoroughly versed in the classics and histories and fit to stand as a model scholar.

sentences.zh: 當世皆榮之。

translations.literal: The age all took it as glory.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded this as the highest honor.

sentences.zh: 帝春秋高，諸王強盛。

translations.literal: The emperor's years were advanced, and the princes were powerful.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor grew old, the princes grew powerful.

sentences.zh: 殷嘗受密命輔皇太孫。

translations.literal: Yin had once received a secret charge to assist the heir apparent's son.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had once received a secret commission to support the heir apparent's son.

sentences.zh: 及燕師日逼，惠帝命殷充總兵官鎮守淮安。

translations.literal: When the Yan army pressed daily closer, Emperor Hui ordered Yin to serve as commander-in-chief and hold Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: As the Yan forces drew nearer day by day, Emperor Hui appointed Yin commander-in-chief to defend Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 悉心防禦，號令嚴明。

translations.literal: He devoted his heart to defense; his commands were strict and clear.
translations.idiomatic: He defended the city with tireless care, and his orders were strict and clear.

sentences.zh: 燕兵破何福軍，執諸將平安等，遣使假道於殷，以進香為名。

translations.literal: The Yan army defeated He Fu's force and captured the generals Ping'an and others; they sent envoys to ask passage through Yin, under the pretext of offering incense.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating He Fu's army and capturing generals including Ping'an, the Yan forces sent envoys to Yin requesting passage, under the pretense of offering incense at a shrine.

sentences.zh: 殷答曰：「進香，皇考有禁，不遵者為不孝。」

translations.literal: Yin replied: "Offering incense—our late father forbade it; whoever does not obey is unfilial."
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied, "Our late father forbade such incense offerings. Whoever disregards that ban is unfilial."

sentences.zh: 王大怒，復書言：「今興兵誅君側惡，天命有歸，非人所能阻。」

translations.literal: The prince was greatly angered and wrote back: "Now I raise the army to punish evil at the ruler's side; Heaven's mandate has its destination—no man can obstruct it."
translations.idiomatic: The prince was furious and wrote back, "I have taken up arms to purge evil from the ruler's side. Heaven's mandate has found its bearer, and no man can stand in its way."

sentences.zh: 殷割使者耳鼻縱之，曰：「留汝口為殿下言君臣大義。」

translations.literal: Yin cut off the envoy's ears and nose and released him, saying: "I leave you your mouth to tell His Highness the great meaning of ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yin cut off the envoy's ears and nose and sent him back, saying, "I leave you your mouth so you may tell His Highness what ruler and subject truly owe each other."

sentences.zh: 王為氣沮。

translations.literal: The prince's spirit was deflated.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's ardor was checked.

sentences.zh: 而鳳陽守徐安亦拆浮橋，絕舟楫以遏燕。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xu An, defender of Fengyang, also dismantled the pontoon bridge and cut off boats to block the Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu An, defender of Fengyang, dismantled the pontoon bridge and blocked river traffic to obstruct the Yan advance.

sentences.zh: 燕兵乃涉泗，出天長，取道揚州。

translations.literal: The Yan army then crossed the Si, emerged at Tianchang, and took the route through Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army forded the Si River, passed through Tianchang, and advanced by way of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，殷尚擁兵淮上，帝迫公主嚙血為書投殷。

translations.literal: When the prince took the throne, Yin still held troops on the Huai; the emperor pressed the princess to write in blood and send it to Yin.
translations.idiomatic: After the prince took the throne, Yin still held an army on the Huai. The new emperor pressed the princess to write a letter in her own blood and send it to Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷得書慟哭，乃還京。

translations.literal: Yin received the letter and wept bitterly, then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wept when he read it and then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既入見，帝迎勞曰：「駙馬勞苦。」

translations.literal: After he entered audience, the emperor came forward to comfort him, saying: "Commandant, you have toiled."
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, the emperor greeted him warmly. "Commandant, you have borne great hardships," he said."

sentences.zh: 殷曰：「勞而無功耳。」

translations.literal: Yin said: "Toiled yet accomplished nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Yin replied, "Hardships borne, but to no avail."

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年，都御史陳瑛奏殷畜養亡命，與女秀才劉氏朋邪詛咒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongle, Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying memorialized that Yin harbored fugitives and, with the female scholar Liu, formed an evil clique to curse by sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 2, Censor-in-Chief Chen Ying reported that Yin was sheltering fugitives and, together with a female scholar surnamed Liu, practicing sorcery and treasonous curses.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕自處之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I myself will deal with it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I shall handle this myself."

sentences.zh: 因諭戶部考定公、侯、駙馬、伯儀仗從人之數，而別命錦衣衛執殷家人送遼東。

translations.literal: He then instructed the Ministry of Revenue to fix the numbers of ceremonial escorts for dukes, marquises, commandants, and earls, while separately ordering the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to seize Yin's household and send them to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Ministry of Revenue to fix the size of ceremonial escorts for dukes, marquises, commandants, and earls, while separately directing the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to seize Yin's household and exile them to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 明年冬十月，殷入朝，前軍都督僉事譚深、錦衣衛指揮趙曦擠殷笪橋下，溺死，以殷自投水聞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following winter Yin came to court; Vice Commissioner Tan Shen of the Forward Army Command and Embroidered-Uniform Guard Director Zhao Xi pushed Yin off the Dadao Bridge, and he drowned; it was announced that Yin had thrown himself into the water.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, in the tenth month, Yin came to court. Tan Shen, vice commissioner of the Forward Army Command, and Zhao Xi, director of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, pushed him off the Dadao Bridge and drowned him. The court announced that Yin had drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 都督同知許成發其事。

translations.literal: Associate Commissioner-in-Chief Xu Cheng exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Commissioner-in-Chief Xu Cheng exposed the crime.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命法司治深、曦罪，斬之，籍其家。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered the judicial offices to try Shen and Xi, behead them, and confiscate their households.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the judicial authorities to try Shen and Xi, execute them, and confiscate their estates.

sentences.zh: 遣官為殷治喪，謚榮定，而封許成為永新伯。

translations.literal: He dispatched officials to arrange Yin's funeral, gave the posthumous title Glorious and Settled, and enfeoffed Xu Cheng as Earl of Yongxin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officials to arrange Yin's funeral, granted him the posthumous title Glorious and Settled, and enfeoffed Xu Cheng as Earl of Yongxin.

sentences.zh: 初，公主聞殷死，謂上果殺殷，牽衣大哭，問駙馬安在。

translations.literal: At first, when the princess heard Yin had died, she believed the emperor had indeed killed Yin; clutching his robe she wept loudly and asked where the commandant was.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess first heard of Yin's death, she assumed the emperor had murdered him. Clutching at his robe, she wept and demanded to know where her husband was.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為主跡賊，無自苦。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In tracking down the culprit for you, do not torment yourself."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am hunting down the culprits on your behalf. Do not torment yourself."

sentences.zh: 尋官殷二子，順昌為中府都督同知，景福為旗手衛指揮使，賜公主書曰：「駙馬殷雖有過失，兄以至親不問。

translations.literal: Soon he appointed Yin's two sons: Shunchang as Associate Commissioner of the Central Military Commission, Jingfu as Director of the Banner-Halberd Guard; he granted the princess a letter saying: "Commandant Yin, though he had faults, I as elder brother did not inquire because of our close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: He soon appointed Yin's two sons—Shunchang as associate commissioner of the Central Military Commission and Jingfu as director of the Banner-Halberd Guard—and wrote the princess: "Though Commandant Yin had faults, I overlooked them because he was my brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 比聞溺死，兄甚疑之。

translations.literal: When I lately heard he drowned, I was greatly suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When I heard he had drowned, I was deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 都督許成來首，已加爵賞，謀害之人悉置重法，特報妹知之。」

translations.literal: Commissioner Xu Cheng came to confess; I have already added rank and reward; those who plotted the murder have all been subjected to severe law—specially reporting this for my younger sister's knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Xu Cheng came forward with a confession. I have already rewarded him with a noble title. Those who plotted the murder have all been punished to the full extent of the law. I write specially to inform you, my sister."

sentences.zh: 瓦剌灰者，降人也，事殷久，謂深、曦實殺殷，請於帝，斷二人手足，剖其腸祭殷，遂自經死。

translations.literal: Wala Hui was a surrendered tribesman who had long served Yin; he said Shen and Xi had truly killed Yin, and begged the emperor to cut off the two men's hands and feet, split open their bellies to sacrifice to Yin, then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wala Hui, a surrendered tribesman who had long served Yin, insisted that Shen and Xi had murdered him. He begged the emperor to cut off their hands and feet and disembowel them as an offering to Yin, then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 十二月進封公主為寧國長公主。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the princess was advanced to Senior Princess of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month she was promoted to Senior Princess of Ning.

sentences.zh: 宣德九年八月薨，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the ninth year of Xuande she passed away, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the eighth month of Xuande year 9, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 初，主聞成祖舉兵，貽書責以大義。

translations.literal: At first, when the princess heard Chengzu had raised the army, she sent a letter rebuking him with the great moral principle.
translations.idiomatic: When she first learned that Chengzu had taken up arms, she wrote to rebuke him on grounds of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 不答。

translations.literal: He did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: He did not answer.

sentences.zh: 成祖至淮北，貽主書，命遷居太平門外，勿罹兵禍。

translations.literal: When Chengzu reached north of the Huai, he sent the princess a letter ordering her to move outside Taiping Gate and not suffer military calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu reached the north bank of the Huai, he wrote urging her to move outside Taiping Gate and keep clear of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 主亦不答。

translations.literal: The princess also did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: She did not answer that either.

sentences.zh: 然成祖故重主，即位後，歲時賜與無算，諸王莫敢望。

translations.literal: Yet Chengzu had always held the princess in esteem; after taking the throne, seasonal gifts and grants were beyond counting—none of the princes dared compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chengzu had always held her in high regard. After his accession, seasonal gifts to her were beyond counting, and none of the princes could compare.

sentences.zh: 殷孫純，成化中舉進士，知定遠縣，忤上官，棄歸。

translations.literal: Yin's grandson Chun, in the Chenghua reign passed the jinshi examination, served as magistrate of Dingyuan County, offended his superiors, and abandoned office to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's grandson Chun passed the jinshi examination in the Chenghua reign, served as magistrate of Dingyuan County, clashed with his superiors, and resigned to return home.

sentences.zh: 襲武階，為中都副留守。

translations.literal: He inherited the military rank and became Deputy Commandant of the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then inherited the family's military rank and became deputy commandant of the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 崇寧公主，洪武十七年下嫁牛城，未幾薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chongning, in the seventeenth year of Hongwu married Niu Cheng and soon passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chongning married Niu Cheng in Hongwu year 17 and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 安慶公主，寧國主母妹。

translations.literal: The Princess of Anqing, younger sister of the mother of the Princess of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Anqing was the younger sister of the Ning princess's mother.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年下嫁歐陽倫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu she married Ouyang Lun.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 14 she married Ouyang Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫頗不法。

translations.literal: Lun was quite lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was notably lawless.

sentences.zh: 洪武末，茶禁方嚴，數遣私人販茶出境，所至繹騷，雖大吏不敢問。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongwu the tea prohibition was especially strict; he repeatedly sent private persons to smuggle tea beyond the borders; wherever they went there was constant disturbance, and even high officials did not dare inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Hongwu reign the tea monopoly was strictly enforced, yet Lun repeatedly sent private agents to smuggle tea across the border. Wherever they went they caused uproar, and even senior officials dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 有家奴周保者尤橫，輒呼有司科民車至數十輛。

translations.literal: There was a household slave Zhou Bao who was especially overbearing; he would summon officials to levy civilian carts up to several tens.
translations.idiomatic: One household slave, Zhou Bao, was especially brutal. He routinely ordered local officials to press civilians into providing dozens of carts at a time.

sentences.zh: 過河橋巡檢司，擅捶辱司吏。

translations.literal: Passing the bridge-inspection office at Hegiao, he arbitrarily beat and insulted the office clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hegiao Bridge inspection office he took it upon himself to beat and humiliate the clerk on duty.

sentences.zh: 吏不堪，以聞。

translations.literal: The clerk could not bear it and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk could endure it no longer and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，賜倫死，保等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, granted Lun death, and Bao and the rest were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Lun was sentenced to death, and Bao and his accomplices were all executed.

sentences.zh: 汝寧公主，洪武十五年與懷慶、大名二主先後下嫁，而主下嫁陸賢，吉安侯仲亨子也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Runing—in the fifteenth year of Hongwu, together with the princesses of Huaiqing and Daming marrying in succession, this princess married Lu Xian, son of Marquis Zhongheng of Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Runing. In Hongwu year 15 she married, in the same period as the princesses of Huaiqing and Daming, Lu Xian, son of Marquis Zhongheng of Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 福清公主，母鄭安妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Fuqing, mother the Consort Zheng An.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Fuqing, daughter of Consort Zheng An.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年下嫁張麟，鳳翔侯龍子也。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Hongwu she married Zhang Lin, son of Marquis Long of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 18 she married Zhang Lin, son of Marquis Long of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 麟未嗣侯卒。

translations.literal: Lin died before he could inherit the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: Lin died before he could inherit his father's title.

sentences.zh: 永樂十五年，主薨。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yongle the princess passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Yongle year 15.

sentences.zh: 壽春公主，洪武十九年下嫁傅忠，穎國公友德子也。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shouchun, in the nineteenth year of Hongwu married Fu Zhong, son of the Duke of Ying, Fu Youde.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shouchun married Fu Zhong in Hongwu year 19. Zhong was the son of Fu Youde, Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 先是，九年二月定制：公主未受封者，歲給纻絲紗絹布線；

translations.literal: Earlier, in the second month of the ninth year regulations were fixed: princesses not yet enfeoffed received annually ramie silk, gauze silk, silk damask, cloth, and thread;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the second month of year 9, regulations were established: an unenfeoffed princess received annual allotments of ramie silk, gauze, damask, cloth, and thread;

sentences.zh: 已封，賜莊田一區，歲征租一千五百石，鈔二千貫。

translations.literal: once enfeoffed, they were granted one estate district, with annual rent collection of fifteen hundred shi and two thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: once enfeoffed, she received an estate yielding fifteen hundred shi in annual rent and two thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 主為太祖所愛，賜吳江縣田一百二十余頃，皆上腴，歲入八千石，逾他主數倍。

translations.literal: The princess was beloved by Taizu; he granted her fields in Wujiang County totaling more than one hundred twenty qing, all of the finest soil, with annual income of eight thousand shi—several times that of other princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu favored this princess and granted her more than one hundred twenty qing of fields in Wujiang County, all prime land yielding eight thousand shi a year—several times the income of her sisters.

sentences.zh: 二十一年薨，賜明器儀杖以葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year she passed away; bright vessels and ceremonial staffs were granted for burial.
translations.idiomatic: She died in year 21, and the court granted funeral regalia and ceremonial staffs for her burial.

sentences.zh: 十公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Tenth Princess died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Tenth Princess died young.

sentences.zh: 永嘉公主，母郭惠妃。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongjia, mother Consort Guo Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongjia, daughter of Consort Guo Hui.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十二年下嫁郭鎮，武定侯英子也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Hongwu she married Guo Zhen, son of Marquis Ying of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 22 she married Guo Zhen, son of Marquis Ying of Wuding.

sentences.zh: 英卒，鎮不得嗣。

translations.literal: When Ying died, Zhen could not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying died, Zhen was unable to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 宣德十年，主乞以子珍嗣，語在《英傳》。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuande the princess begged that her son Zhen might inherit; the account is in the 《Biography of Ying》.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande year 10 the princess petitioned that her son Zhen be allowed to inherit; the matter is recorded in the 《Biography of Ying》.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年，主薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai the princess passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Jingtai year 6.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，元孫勛有寵，為主乞追謚，特賜謚貞懿。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, the great-grandson Xun was favored and begged a posthumous title for the princess; she was specially granted the posthumous title Chaste and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's accession, her great-grandson Xun, then in favor at court, petitioned for a posthumous title on her behalf. She was specially granted the name Chaste and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 十三公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Thirteenth Princess died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Thirteenth Princess died young.

sentences.zh: 含山公主，母高麗妃韓氏。

translations.literal: The Princess of Hanshan, mother the Goryeo consort Lady Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Hanshan, daughter of the Goryeo consort Lady Han.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十七年下嫁尹清。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Hongwu she married Yin Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 27 she married Yin Qing.

sentences.zh: 建文初，清掌後府都督事，先主卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwen, Qing directed the Rear Palace military commission affairs and died before the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianwen reign Qing directed affairs of the Rear Palace military commission and died before the princess.

sentences.zh: 主至天順六年始薨，年八十有二。

translations.literal: The princess lived until the sixth year of Tianshun before passing away, aged eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The princess lived until Tianshun year 6, dying at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 汝陽公主，永嘉主同母妹，與含山主同年下嫁謝達。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ruyang, younger sister by the same mother as the Princess of Yongjia, married Xie Da in the same year as the Princess of Hanshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ruyang, younger sister of the Yongjia princess by the same mother, married Xie Da in the same year as the Hanshan princess.

sentences.zh: 達父彥，鳳陽人，少育於孫氏，冒其姓。

translations.literal: Da's father Yan was a man of Fengyang; raised young by the Sun clan, he took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: Da's father Yan was from Fengyang. Raised in youth by the Sun clan, he had taken their surname.

sentences.zh: 數從征討有功，累官前軍都督僉事，詔復謝姓，遷其子尚主。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed campaigns with merit, rose to Vice Commissioner of the Forward Army Command, was ordered to resume the Xie surname, and his son was advanced to marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned repeatedly with distinction and rose to vice commissioner of the Forward Army Command. An edict restored the Xie surname, and his son was promoted to marry the princess.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，主以屬尊，與寧國、懷慶、大名、南康、永嘉、含山、寶慶七主皆進稱大長公主。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, because of her senior kinship the princess, together with the seven princesses of Ning, Huaiqing, Daming, Nankang, Yongjia, Hanshan, and Baoqing, were all advanced to the title Grand Senior Princess.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong took the throne, this princess and seven others—of Ning, Huaiqing, Daming, Nankang, Yongjia, Hanshan, and Baoqing—were all promoted to Grand Senior Princess on account of their senior rank.

sentences.zh: 自後諸帝即位，公主進封長公主、大長公主皆如制。

translations.literal: From then on, whenever emperors took the throne, princesses' advancement to Senior Princess and Grand Senior Princess all followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever a new emperor took the throne, princesses were promoted to Senior Princess or Grand Senior Princess according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 寶慶公主，太祖最幼女，下嫁趙輝。

translations.literal: The Princess of Baoqing, Taizu's youngest daughter, married Zhao Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Baoqing, Taizu's youngest daughter, married Zhao Hui.

sentences.zh: 輝父和以千戶從征安南陣沒，輝襲父官。

translations.literal: Hui's father He followed the campaign to Annam as a chiliarch and died in battle; Hui inherited his father's office.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's father He had served as a chiliarch in the Annam campaign and died in battle. Hui inherited his father's post.

sentences.zh: 先是，成祖即位，主甫八歲，命仁孝皇后撫之如女。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chengzu took the throne, the princess was only eight; he ordered Empress Renxiao to rear her as a daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu took the throne the princess was only eight. He ordered Empress Renxiao to raise her as her own daughter.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年，輝以千戶守金川門，年二十余，狀貌偉麗，遂選以尚主。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle, Hui as chiliarch guarded the Jinchuan Gate; aged a little over twenty, of imposing appearance, he was selected to marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 11 Hui, a chiliarch guarding Jinchuan Gate, was in his early twenties and strikingly handsome. He was chosen to marry the princess.

sentences.zh: 主既為後所撫，裝賫視他主倍渥，婚夕特詔皇太子送入邸。

translations.literal: Since the princess had been reared by the empress, her trousseau was twice as rich as other princesses'; on the wedding night a special edict ordered the crown prince to escort her to the residence.
translations.idiomatic: Because the empress had raised her, her trousseau was twice as lavish as that of other princesses. On the wedding night a special edict directed the crown prince to escort her to the residence.

sentences.zh: 主性純淑，宣德八年薨。

translations.literal: The princess was pure and gentle in nature; in the eighth year of Xuande she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was gentle and virtuous by nature. She died in Xuande year 8.

sentences.zh: 輝至成化十二年始卒。

translations.literal: Hui lived until the twelfth year of Chenghua before dying.
translations.idiomatic: Hui did not die until Chenghua year 12.

sentences.zh: 凡事六朝，歷掌南京都督及宗人府事。

translations.literal: He served six reigns in all, and successively directed Nanjing military commission and Imperial Clan Court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served six reigns and at various times directed both the Nanjing military commission and the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 家故豪侈，姬妾至百余人，享有富貴者六十余年，壽九十。

translations.literal: His household was by nature extravagant; his concubines reached more than a hundred; he enjoyed wealth and honor for more than sixty years and lived to ninety.
translations.idiomatic: His household was famously extravagant, with more than a hundred concubines. He enjoyed wealth and privilege for more than sixty years and lived to ninety.

sentences.zh: 附福成、慶陽二主

translations.literal: Appended: the two princesses of Fucheng and Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Appended: the Princesses of Fucheng and Qingyang

sentences.zh: 福成公主，南昌王女，母王氏。

translations.literal: The Princess of Fucheng, daughter of the Prince of Nanchang, mother Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Fucheng, daughter of the Prince of Nanchang and Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 嫁王克恭。

translations.literal: She married Wang Kejing.
translations.idiomatic: She married Wang Kejing.

sentences.zh: 克恭嘗為福建行省參政，後改福州衛指揮使。

translations.literal: Kejing had served as Administrative Commissioner of Fujian Province, later transferred to Director of the Fuzhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing had served as administrative commissioner of Fujian Province and later became director of the Fuzhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 興宗四女

translations.literal: Four daughters of the Progenitor of the Revival.
translations.idiomatic: The Progenitor of the Revival's four daughters

sentences.zh: 宜倫郡主，永樂十五年下嫁於禮。

translations.literal: The Commandery Mistress of Yilun, in the fifteenth year of Yongle married Yu Li.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandery Mistress of Yilun married Yu Li in Yongle year 15.

sentences.zh: 三女，無考。

translations.literal: Three daughters, no record.
translations.idiomatic: Three daughters; no further record survives.

sentences.zh: 南平郡主，未下嫁，永樂十年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Commandery Mistress of Nanping, not yet married, passed away in the tenth year of Yongle and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandery Mistress of Nanping died unmarried in Yongle year 10 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 成祖五女

translations.literal: Five daughters of Chengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu's five daughters

sentences.zh: 永安公主，下嫁袁容。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yong'an married Yuan Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yong'an married Yuan Rong.

sentences.zh: 容，壽州人，父洪以開國功，官都督。

translations.literal: Rong was a man of Shouzhou; his father Hong, for founding merit, held the office of commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was from Shouzhou. His father Hong, a founding meritocrat, held the rank of commissioner.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十八年選容為燕府儀賓，配永安郡主。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Hongwu Rong was selected as Ceremonial Guest of the Prince of Yan's establishment, matched to the Commandery Mistress of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 28 Rong was chosen as Ceremonial Guest to the Prince of Yan and betrothed to the Commandery Mistress of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 燕兵起，有戰守功。

translations.literal: When the Yan army rose, he had merit in fighting and defending.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces took up arms, he distinguished himself in attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 永樂元年進郡主為公主，容駙馬都尉；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongle the commandery mistress was advanced to princess, and Rong became Commandant of Horse Escort;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 1 the commandery mistress was promoted to princess and Rong became Commandant of Horse Escort;

sentences.zh: 再論功，封廣平侯，祿一千五百石，予世券。

translations.literal: merits were again weighed and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangping, stipend one thousand five hundred shi, granted a hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: his merits were weighed again and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangping with a stipend of fifteen hundred shi and a hereditary patent.

sentences.zh: 凡車駕巡幸，皆命容居守。

translations.literal: Whenever the imperial carriage toured, Rong was always ordered to remain and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled, Rong was left in charge of the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，都指揮款臺乘馬過容門，容怒其不下，棰之幾死。

translations.literal: At first, Regional Commander Kuantai rode his horse past Rong's gate; Rong was angry he did not dismount and beat him nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once Regional Commander Kuantai rode past Rong's gate without dismounting. Rong was furious and beat him nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，賜趙王高燧書曰：「自洪武來，往來駙馬門者，未聞令下馬也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he sent the Prince of Zhao, Gao Sui, a letter saying: "Since Hongwu, those passing commandants' gates have not been heard to be ordered to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he wrote to the Prince of Zhao, Gao Sui: "Since the Hongwu reign, no one passing a commandant's gate has been required to dismount.

sentences.zh: 昔晉王敦為駙馬，縱恣暴橫，卒以滅亡。

translations.literal: In old times Wang Dun of Jin was a commandant and indulged in wanton violence; in the end he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun of Jin had once been a commandant and indulged in wanton violence until he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 汝其以書示容，令械辱款臺之人送京師。」

translations.literal: You shall show Rong this letter and order the men who shackled and insulted Kuantai sent to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Show Rong this letter and send the men who shackled and humiliated Kuantai to the capital in bonds.

sentences.zh: 容由是斂戢。

translations.literal: Rong thereby restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Rong thereafter restrained himself.

sentences.zh: 十五年，主薨，停容侯祿。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the princess passed away; Rong's marquis stipend was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 the princess died and Rong's marquis stipend was suspended.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，復故。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, it was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong took the throne, the stipend was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈沂國公，謚忠穆。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Yi, posthumous title Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yi with the temple name Loyal and Solemn.

sentences.zh: 子禎嗣，卒，無子。

translations.literal: His son Zhen inherited, died, and had no son.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen inherited the title but died without an heir.

sentences.zh: 庶弟瑄，正統初乞嗣。

translations.literal: The younger brother by a concubine, Xuan, at the beginning of Zhengtong begged to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His younger half-brother Xuan petitioned to inherit early in the Zhengtong reign.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「容封以公主恩，禎嗣以公主子。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Rong's enfeoffment was through the princess's grace; Zhen's inheritance was as the princess's son.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Rong's title was granted through the princess's favor; Zhen inherited as her son.

sentences.zh: 瑄庶子，可長陵衛指揮僉事。」

translations.literal: Xuan is a son by a concubine; he may be Vice Director of the Changling Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan is a son by a concubine. Let him be vice director of the Changling Guard.

sentences.zh: 天順元年詔復侯爵，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshun an edict restored the marquisate; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshun year 1 an edict restored the marquisate. He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 弟琇，成化十五年嗣，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiu inherited in the fifteenth year of Chenghua and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiu inherited in Chenghua year 15 and died.

sentences.zh: 侄輅乞嗣侯，言官持不可。

translations.literal: The nephew Lu begged to inherit the marquisate; remonstrating officials held it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The nephew Lu petitioned to inherit the marquisate, but remonstrating officials objected.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「詔書許子孫嗣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The edict patent permitted descendants to inherit.

translations.idiomatic: The princess was respectful, discreet, and observant of ritual, and was versed in the 《Classic of Filial Piety》 and the 《Rules for Women》.

translations.idiomatic: Renzong's seven daughters

translations.idiomatic: Jing was from Changli.

translations.idiomatic: She died in Hongzhi year 12.

sentences.zh: 淳安公主，成化二年下嫁蔡震。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chun'an, in the second year of Chenghua married Cai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chun'an married Cai Zhen in Chenghua year 2.

sentences.zh: 震行醇謹。

translations.literal: Zhen's conduct was pure and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was upright and discreet in conduct.

sentences.zh: 正德中，劉瑾下獄，詔廷訊。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign Liu Jin was imprisoned; an edict ordered trial at court.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign Liu Jin was imprisoned and the court ordered a public interrogation.

sentences.zh: 有問者，瑾輒指其人附己，廷臣無敢詰。

translations.literal: When questioned, Jin would point at someone as having joined him; court ministers did not dare press further.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever questioned, Jin would point at someone and claim him as an accomplice, and the ministers at court dared not press further.

sentences.zh: 震歷聲曰：「我皇家至戚，應不附爾！」

translations.literal: Zhen raised his voice and said: "I am the imperial clan's closest kin—surely I would not join you!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen spoke up loudly: "I am the emperor's closest kin by marriage—I would never have joined you!

sentences.zh: 趣獄卒考掠之，瑾乃服罪，以是知名。

translations.literal: He urged the prison guards to torture him; Jin then confessed guilt, and by this became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the guards to torture him instead. Jin then confessed, and Zhen became famous for this act.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中卒，贈太保，謚康僖。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign he died; he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and posthumous title Healthy and Gracious.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Jiajing reign and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian with the temple name Healthy and Gracious.

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chongde, daughter of Consort Yang An.

translations.idiomatic: She died in Hongzhi year 2.

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guangde, daughter of Consort Wan Chen.

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiaxiang, daughter of Consort Lady Liu.

translations.idiomatic: She died six years later.

translations.idiomatic: The Jing Emperor's one daughter

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Gu'an. When Yingzong was restored to the throne, her title was reduced to Commandery Mistress.

sentences.zh: 成化時，年已長，憲宗以閣臣奏，五年十一月下嫁王憲。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign she was already advanced in years; Xianzong, on the memorial of grand secretaries, in the eleventh month of the fifth year had her marry Wang Xian.
translations.idiomatic: By the Chenghua reign she was already elderly. On the grand secretaries' recommendation, Xianzong had her marry Wang Xian in the eleventh month of year 5.

sentences.zh: 禮儀視公主，以故尚書蹇義賜第賜之。

translations.literal: Ceremonial observances were as for a princess; the former Minister Jian Yi was granted a residence and it was bestowed on her.
translations.idiomatic: She was accorded the ceremonial honors of a princess, and the former residence of Minister Jian Yi was granted to her.

sentences.zh: 憲宗五女

translations.literal: Five daughters of Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong's five daughters

sentences.zh: 永康公主，弘治六年下嫁崔元。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongkang, in the sixth year of Hongzhi married Cui Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongkang married Cui Yuan in Hongzhi year 6.

sentences.zh: 元，代州人，世宗入繼，以迎立功封京山侯，給誥券。

translations.literal: Yuan was a man of Daizhou; when Shizong entered the succession, for merit in welcoming him he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingshan and granted a patent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was from Daizhou. When Shizong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingshan for his service in welcoming the new emperor and granted a patent of appointment.

sentences.zh: 禮部言：「奉迎乃臣子之分，遽膺封爵，無故事。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites said: "Welcoming the emperor is a subject's duty; to suddenly receive enfeoffment has no precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites objected: "Welcoming the emperor is merely a subject's duty. There is no precedent for enfeoffment on that account alone.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「永樂初年，太宗入繼大統，駙馬都尉王寧以翊戴功封永春侯，何得言無故事。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the early years of Yongle, when Taizong entered the great succession, Commandant Wang Ning was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchun for supporting the enthronement—how can one say there is no precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "In the early Yongle reign, when Taizong took the throne, Commandant Wang Ning was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongchun for supporting his accession. How can you say there is no precedent?"

sentences.zh: 給事中底蘊、御史高越等連章論其不可。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Di Yun, Censor Gao Yue, and others submitted successive memorials arguing it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Di Yun, censor Gao Yue, and others submitted repeated memorials arguing against it.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽。

translations.literal: All were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 已，坐張延齡事下詔獄，尋釋。

translations.literal: Later, on account of the Zhang Yanling affair he was sent to the imperial prison, then soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was imprisoned over the Zhang Yanling affair but was soon released.

sentences.zh: 元好交文士，播聲譽，寵幸優渥，勛臣戚畹莫敢望焉。

translations.literal: Yuan loved to associate with literary men, spread his reputation, enjoyed lavish favor—no meritorious minister or imperial affinal kin dared compare.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan cultivated literary circles, built his reputation, and enjoyed lavish favor at court such that no meritorious minister or imperial in-law dared rival him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十八年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiajing year 28.

sentences.zh: 贈左柱國太傅兼太子太傅，謚榮恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Glorious and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Pillar of the State, Grand Tutor, and concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, with the temple name Glorious and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 駙馬封侯贈官不以軍功自元始。

translations.literal: A commandant's enfeoffment as marquis and posthumous offices not based on military merit began with Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuan onward, commandants were enfeoffed as marquises and granted posthumous offices without military merit.

sentences.zh: 主先元薨。

translations.literal: The princess died before Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The princess died before Yuan.

sentences.zh: 長泰公主，成化二十三年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changtai passed away in the twenty-third year of Chenghua and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Changtai died in Chenghua year 23 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 仙遊公主，弘治五年薨，追冊。

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Xianyou died in Hongzhi year 5 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

translations.literal: Three daughters of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong's three daughters

translations.literal: The Princess of Taikang passed away in the eleventh year of Hongzhi, not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taikang died unmarried in Hongzhi year 11.

sentences.zh: 永福公主，嘉靖二年下嫁鄔景和。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongfu, in the second year of Jiajing married Wu Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongfu married Wu Jinghe in Jiajing year 2.

sentences.zh: 景和，昆山人，嘗奉旨直西苑，撰玄文，以不諳玄理辭。

translations.literal: Jinghe was a man of Kunshan; he had been ordered to serve duty at the Western Park and compose arcane texts, but declined on grounds of not understanding arcane principles.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe was from Kunshan. He had been ordered to serve at the Western Park and compose arcane texts, but declined on the grounds that he did not understand such doctrines.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 時有事清馥殿，在直諸臣俱行祝厘禮，景和不俟禮成而出。

translations.literal: At the time there was a ceremony at the Qingfu Hall; all ministers on duty performed the blessing rite, but Jinghe left before the rite was completed.
translations.idiomatic: When a blessing ceremony was held at the Qingfu Hall, all ministers on duty performed the rite, but Jinghe left before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 已而賞賚諸臣，景和與焉。

translations.literal: Later rewards were bestowed on the ministers, and Jinghe was included.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were later distributed to the ministers, Jinghe was included.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「無功受賞，懼增罪戾。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Receiving reward without merit, I fear increases guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I have received reward without merit and fear this only deepens my guilt.

sentences.zh: 乞容辭免，俾洗心滌慮，以效他日馬革裹屍、啣環結草之報。」

translations.literal: I beg permission to decline, that I may cleanse heart and thoughts, to repay in future days with death wrapped in horsehide and the knotted-grass debt of gratitude."
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to decline, so that I may purify my heart and thoughts and one day repay Your Majesty with my life on the battlefield and the gratitude owed even from beyond the grave.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，謂詛咒失人臣禮，削職歸原籍，時主已薨矣。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, saying he had cursed and failed the minister's rites; his office was stripped and he returned to his native place—the princess had already passed away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, declaring that his words amounted to a curse and violated a subject's duty. Jinghe was stripped of office and sent home. The princess had already died.

sentences.zh: 三十五年入賀聖誕畢，因言：「臣自五世祖寄籍錦衣衛，世居北地。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, having finished congratulating the imperial birthday, he said: "From my fifth-generation ancestor my household was registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard; we have long dwelt in the north.
translations.idiomatic: In year 35, after attending the imperial birthday celebration, he said: "Since my fifth-generation ancestor our household has been registered with the Embroidered-Uniform Guard and has long lived in the north.

sentences.zh: 今被罪南徙，不勝犬馬戀主之私。

translations.literal: Now condemned and moved south, I cannot overcome the private longing of dog and horse for their master.
translations.idiomatic: Now condemned and sent south, I cannot overcome my loyal longing for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 扶服入賀，退而私省公主墳墓，丘封翳然，荊棘不剪。

translations.literal: In mourning garb I came to congratulate; afterward I privately visited the princess's tomb—the mound overgrown, brambles uncut.
translations.idiomatic: I came in mourning garb to offer congratulations, then privately visited the princess's tomb. The mound was overgrown and the brambles untrimmed.

sentences.zh: 臣切自念，狐死尚正首丘，臣托命貴主，獨與逝者魂魄相吊於數千里外，不得春秋祭掃，拊心傷悔，五內崩裂。

translations.literal: I deeply reflect: even a fox at death turns its head toward its mound; I entrusted my life to the noble princess, yet alone mourn the departed spirit thousands of li away, unable to perform spring and autumn sacrifices—beating my breast in grief and remorse, my five viscera rent asunder.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect deeply that even a fox turns its head toward its home mound at death. I entrusted my life to the noble princess, yet I mourn her spirit alone thousands of li away, unable to perform the spring and autumn sacrifices. My heart is torn with grief and remorse.

sentences.zh: 臣之罪重，不敢祈恩，惟陛下幸哀故主，使得寄籍原衛，長與相依，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: My guilt is heavy; I dare not beg grace—only that Your Majesty pity my late mistress and permit me to register again with my original guard, to dwell long beside her, and die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: My guilt is grave and I dare not beg favor. I ask only that Your Majesty pity my late mistress and permit me to register again with my original guard, to remain near her always, and die without regret.

sentences.zh: 帝憐而許之。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年復官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longqing his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His office was restored in Longqing year 2.

sentences.zh: 卒贈少保，謚榮簡。

translations.literal: At death he was granted Junior Guardian, posthumous title Glorious and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted Junior Guardian with the temple name Glorious and Simple.

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongchun married Xie Zhao.

translations.idiomatic: Ruizong's two daughters

translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shanhua died young.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing,
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 4,

sentences.zh: 〈（長寧、善化）〉

translations.literal: (Changning and Shanhua)〉
translations.idiomatic: Changning and Shanhua)〉

sentences.zh: 二主同日追冊。

translations.literal: the two princesses were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: the two princesses were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 世宗五女

translations.literal: Five daughters of Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's five daughters

sentences.zh: 常安公主，未下嫁。

translations.literal: The Princess of Chang'an, not yet married.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Chang'an had not yet married.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十八年薨，追冊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Jiajing she passed away and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Jiajing year 28 and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 思柔公主，後常安主二月薨，年十二，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Sirou, two months after the Princess of Chang'an passed away, aged twelve, was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Sirou died two months after the Chang'an princess, at the age of twelve, and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 寧安公主，嘉靖三十四年下嫁李和。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ning'an, in the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing married Li He.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ning'an married Li He in Jiajing year 34.

sentences.zh: 歸善公主，嘉靖二十三年薨，追冊，葬祭視太康主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Guishan passed away in the twenty-third year of Jiajing and was posthumously enfeoffed; burial and sacrifices followed the Princess of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Guishan died in Jiajing year 23 and was posthumously enfeoffed. Her burial and sacrifices followed those of the Taikang princess.

sentences.zh: 嘉善公主，嘉靖三十六年下嫁許從誠。

translations.literal: The Princess of Jiashan, in the thirty-sixth year of Jiajing married Xu Congcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Jiashan married Xu Congcheng in Jiajing year 36.

sentences.zh: 四十三年薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in year 43.

sentences.zh: 穆宗六女

translations.literal: Six daughters of Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong's six daughters

sentences.zh: 蓬萊公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Penglai died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Penglai died young.

sentences.zh: 太和公主，早薨。

translations.literal: The Princess of Taihe died early.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Taihe died young.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年與蓬萊主同日追冊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing she and the Princess of Penglai were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In Longqing year 1 she and the Penglai princess were posthumously enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 壽陽公主，萬歷九年下嫁侯拱辰。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shouyang, in the ninth year of Wanli married Hou Gongchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shouyang married Hou Gongchen in Wanli year 9.

sentences.zh: 國本議起，拱辰掌宗人府，亦具疏力爭。

translations.literal: When the succession debate arose, Gongchen directed the Imperial Clan Court and also submitted a memorial arguing forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When the debate over the heir apparent arose, Gongchen, as director of the Imperial Clan Court, submitted a forceful memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 卒贈太傅，謚榮康。

translations.literal: At death he was granted Grand Tutor, posthumous title Glorious and Healthy.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was granted Grand Tutor with the temple name Glorious and Healthy.

sentences.zh: 永寧公主，下嫁梁邦瑞。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yongning married Liang Bangrui.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yongning married Liang Bangrui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年薨。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli she passed away.
translations.idiomatic: She died in Wanli year 35.

sentences.zh: 瑞安公主，神宗同母妹。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ruian, younger sister by the same mother as Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ruian, Shenzong's younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十三年下嫁萬煒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Wanli she married Wan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli year 13 she married Wan Wei.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，主累加大長公主。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign the princess was repeatedly advanced to Grand Senior Princess.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign she was repeatedly promoted to Grand Senior Princess.

sentences.zh: 所產子及庶子長祚、弘祚皆官都督。

translations.literal: Her sons by birth and the sons by concubines Changzuo and Hongzuo all held the office of commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Her sons and her stepsons Changzuo and Hongzuo all held the rank of commissioner.

sentences.zh: 煒官至太傅，管宗人府印。

translations.literal: Wei rose to Grand Tutor and held the seal of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei rose to Grand Tutor and held the seal of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 嘗以親臣侍經筵，每文華進講，佩刀入直。

translations.literal: He had served the classics lecture as an intimate minister; whenever lectures were given at Wenhua, he entered duty wearing his sword.
translations.idiomatic: He had served at the classics lecture as an intimate minister and entered Wenhua Hall for lectures wearing his sword.

sentences.zh: 李建泰西征，命煒以太牢告廟，年七十余矣。

translations.literal: When Li Jiantai marched west, Wei was ordered to announce at the temple with the great sacrifice—he was already over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jiantai marched west, Wei, though already in his seventies, was ordered to announce the campaign at the ancestral temple with the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 國變，同子長祚死於賊。

translations.literal: At the dynastic collapse, he and his son Changzuo died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty fell, he and his son Changzuo were killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 弘祚投水死，長祚妻李氏亦赴井死。

translations.literal: Hongzuo threw himself into the water and died; Changzuo's wife Lady Li also went to a well and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo drowned himself, and Changzuo's wife Lady Li threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 延慶公主，萬歷十五年下嫁王昺。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yanqing, in the fifteenth year of Wanli married Wang Bing.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yanqing married Wang Bing in Wanli year 15.

sentences.zh: 昺嘗救御史劉光復，觸帝怒，削職。

translations.literal: Bing had once rescued Censor Liu Guangfu, provoking the emperor's anger; his office was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Bing had once rescued Censor Liu Guangfu, provoking the emperor's anger, and was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，復官。

translations.literal: When Guangzong took the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong took the throne, his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 神宗十女

translations.literal: Ten daughters of Shenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong's ten daughters

sentences.zh: 榮昌公主，萬歷二十四年下嫁楊春元。

translations.literal: The Princess of Rongchang, in the twenty-fourth year of Wanli married Yang Chunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Rongchang married Yang Chunyuan in Wanli year 24.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，春元卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year Chunyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyuan died in year 44.

sentences.zh: 久之，主薨。

translations.literal: Long afterward the princess passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the princess died as well.

sentences.zh: 壽寧公主，二十七年下嫁冉興讓。

translations.literal: The Princess of Shouning, in the twenty-seventh year married Ran Xingrang.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Shouning married Ran Xingrang in year 27.

sentences.zh: 主為神宗所愛，命五日一來朝，恩澤異他主。

translations.literal: The princess was beloved by Shenzong; he ordered her to attend court once every five days—her favors differed from other princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzong favored this princess and ordered her to attend court every five days. Her privileges exceeded those of all other princesses.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，洛陽失守，莊烈帝命興讓同太監王裕民、給事中葉高標往慰福世子於河北。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, when Luoyang fell, the Zhuanglie Emperor ordered Xingrang together with Eunuch Wang Yumin and Supervising Secretary Ye Gaobiao to go comfort the Heir of Fortune in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, after Luoyang fell, the Zhuanglie Emperor sent Xingrang together with Eunuch Wang Yumin and Supervising Secretary Ye Gaobiao to comfort the Heir of Fortune in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 都城陷，興讓死於賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Xingrang died at the hands of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Xingrang was killed by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 靜樂、雲和、雲夢、靈丘、仙居、泰順、香山、天臺八公主，皆早世，追冊。

translations.literal: The eight princesses of Jingle, Yunhe, Yunmeng, Lingqiu, Xianju, Taishun, Xiangshan, and Tiantai all died young and were posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The eight princesses of Jingle, Yunhe, Yunmeng, Lingqiu, Xianju, Taishun, Xiangshan, and Tiantai all died in infancy and were posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 光宗九女

translations.literal: Nine daughters of Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzong's nine daughters

sentences.zh: 懷淑公主，七歲而薨，追冊。

translations.literal: The Princess of Huaishu passed away at seven and was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Huaishu died at the age of seven and was posthumously enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 餘五女皆早世，未封。

translations.literal: The remaining five daughters all died young and were not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining five daughters all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 寧德公主，下嫁劉有福。

translations.literal: The Princess of Ningde married Liu Youfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Ningde married Liu Youfu.

sentences.zh: 樂安公主，下嫁鞏永固。

translations.literal: The Princess of Le'an married Gong Yonggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Le'an married Gong Yonggu.

sentences.zh: 永固，字洪圖，宛平人，好讀書，負才氣。

translations.literal: Yonggu, style name Hongtu, was a man of Wanping; he loved reading and possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu, courtesy name Hongtu, was from Wanping. He loved reading and was gifted with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年二月，帝召公、侯、伯於德政殿，言：「祖制，勛臣駙馬入監讀書，習武經弓馬。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year of Chongzhen the emperor summoned dukes, marquises, and earls to the Hall of Virtuous Governance, saying: "By ancestral institution, meritorious ministers' sons and commandants enter the Directorate to study, learning military classics, bow, and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Chongzhen year 16 the emperor summoned dukes, marquises, and earls to the Hall of Virtuous Governance and said, "By ancestral institution, the sons of meritorious ministers and commandants enter the Directorate to study the military classics and train in archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 諸臣各有子弟否？」

translations.literal: Do you ministers each have sons and younger brothers?"
translations.idiomatic: Do any of you have sons or younger brothers?

sentences.zh: 成國公朱純臣、定國公徐允禎等皆以幼對。

translations.literal: Duke Zhu Chunchen of Cheng, Duke Xu Yunzhen of Ding, and others all answered that they were still young.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Zhu Chunchen of Cheng, Duke Xu Yunzhen of Ding, and others replied that their sons were still too young.

sentences.zh: 而永固獨上疏，請肄業太學。

translations.literal: Yonggu alone submitted a memorial requesting to pursue studies at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggu alone submitted a memorial requesting to study at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 帝褒答之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and answered him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him in reply.

sentences.zh: 總督趙光抃以邊事系獄，特疏申救。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Zhao Guangbian was imprisoned on border affairs, he specially memorialized to plead for his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor-General Zhao Guangbian was imprisoned over border affairs, Yonggu submitted a special memorial pleading for his release.

sentences.zh: 又請復建文皇帝廟謚。

translations.literal: He also requested restoration of the temple and posthumous title of Emperor Jianwen.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to restore the temple and posthumous title of Emperor Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 事雖未行，時論韙焉。

translations.literal: Though the matters were not carried out, contemporary opinion approved them.
translations.idiomatic: Though neither proposal was adopted, contemporary opinion approved of both.

sentences.zh: 甲申春，賊破宣、大，李邦華請太子南遷，為異議所格。

translations.literal: In the spring of jiashen the rebels took Xuan and Da; Li Banghua requested the crown prince's southward relocation, but was blocked by dissenting opinion.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of jiashen year the rebels captured Xuanfu and Datong. Li Banghua urged the crown prince to relocate south, but dissenting opinion blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 及事急，帝密召永固及新樂侯劉文炳護行。

translations.literal: When matters grew urgent, the emperor secretly summoned Yonggu and Marquis Liu Wenbing of Xinle to escort the journey.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened, the emperor secretly summoned Yonggu and Marquis Liu Wenbing of Xinle to escort the crown prince south.

sentences.zh: 叩頭言：「親臣不藏甲，臣等難以空手搏賊。」

translations.literal: They kowtowed and said: "Intimate ministers do not keep armor; we find it hard to fight rebels empty-handed."
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and said, "As intimate ministers we are not permitted to keep arms. We cannot fight the rebels empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 皆相向涕泣。

translations.literal: All faced one another weeping.
translations.idiomatic: All wept facing one another.

sentences.zh: 十九日，都城陷。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the nineteenth day the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 時公主已薨，未葬，永固以黃繩縛子女五人系柩旁，曰：「此帝甥也，不可汙賊手。」

translations.literal: The princess had already passed away and was not yet buried; Yonggu bound his five children with yellow cord beside the coffin, saying: "These are the emperor's kin by marriage—they must not be defiled by rebel hands."
translations.idiomatic: The princess had already died and was not yet buried. Yonggu bound his five children with yellow cord beside the coffin and said, "These are the emperor's kin by marriage. They must not fall into rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 舉劍自刎，闔室自焚死。

translations.literal: He raised his sword and cut his throat; the whole household burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: He then ran himself through with his sword, and the entire household burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 熹宗二女

translations.literal: Two daughters of Xizong.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong's two daughters

sentences.zh: 皆早世。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: Both died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝六女

translations.literal: Six daughters of the Zhuanglie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuanglie Emperor's six daughters

sentences.zh: 坤儀公主，周皇后生。

translations.literal: The Princess of Kunyi, born to Empress Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Kunyi, daughter of Empress Zhou.

sentences.zh: 追謚。

translations.literal: Posthumous title granted.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 長平公主，年十六，帝選周顯尚主。

translations.literal: The Princess of Changping, aged sixteen; the emperor selected Zhou Xian to marry the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Changping was sixteen when the emperor chose Zhou Xian as her husband.

sentences.zh: 將婚，以寇警暫停。

translations.literal: When the wedding was imminent, it was temporarily halted on account of bandit alarms.
translations.idiomatic: The wedding was imminent but was postponed because of rebel alarms.

sentences.zh: 城陷，帝入壽寧宮，主牽帝衣哭。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the emperor entered the Palace of Longevity and Tranquility; the princess clutched his robe and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the emperor entered the Palace of Longevity and Tranquility. The princess clutched his robe and wept.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝何故生我家！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why were you born into my house!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cried, "Why were you born into this house!

sentences.zh: 以劍揮斫之，斷左臂；

translations.literal: He swung his sword and struck her, severing her left arm;
translations.idiomatic: He swung his sword and struck her, severing her left arm.

sentences.zh: 又斫昭仁公主於昭仁殿。

translations.literal: he also struck down the Princess of Zhaoren in the Hall of Zhaoren.
translations.idiomatic: He then struck down the Princess of Zhaoren in Zhaoren Hall.

sentences.zh: 越五日，長平主復蘇。

translations.literal: Five days later the Princess of Changping revived.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later the Changping princess revived.

sentences.zh: 大清順治二年上書言：「九死臣妾，蹐高天，願髡緇空王，稍申罔極。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi of the Great Qing she submitted a letter saying: "Nine-deaths subject and concubine, treading the high heaven, I wish to shave my head and enter the empty king's realm, slightly to express boundless grief."
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi year 2 of the Great Qing she submitted a letter: "I am a subject who has survived nine deaths, yet I still tread beneath heaven's height. I wish to shave my head and enter the Buddhist order, that I may in some small measure express my boundless grief.

sentences.zh: 詔不許，命顯復尚故主，土田邸第金錢車馬錫予有加。

translations.literal: An edict did not permit it; Xian was ordered again to marry the former princess; fields, residences, money, carriages, and horses were bestowed with additions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused her request and ordered Xian to marry her again. Fields, residences, money, carriages, and horses were bestowed upon them in abundance.

sentences.zh: 主涕泣。

translations.literal: The princess wept with tears.
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 逾年病卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later she died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later she died of illness.

sentences.zh: 賜葬廣寧門外。

translations.literal: Burial was granted outside Guangning Gate.
translations.idiomatic: She was granted burial outside Guangning Gate.

sentences.zh: 餘三女，皆早世，無考。

translations.literal: The remaining three daughters all died young; no record.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining three daughters all died in infancy; no further record survives.
